A patient with established Crohn disease presents with acute-onset gait ataxia (described as “drunk-like” unsteadiness), without associated sensory, cognitive, bulbar, or bladder symptoms. Neuroimaging reveals characteristic findings: multifocal, non-enhancing white matter lesions on T1- and T2-weighted MRI — highly consistent with **Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML)**.

PML is a rare, often fatal demyelinating disorder caused by reactivation of the John Cunningham (JC) virus in the setting of cellular immune deficiency. In patients with inflammatory bowel disease, chronic immunosuppression (e.g., with thiopurines, methotrexate, or biologic agents) is the principal risk factor.

- Serum vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol)
